root_motivation: Who: the operator of prod mcphost, whose tenant table holds every tenant any passer-by ever minted; the human behind an abandoned agent, who today is never told their agent's backend is going away; and real users, who must never lose a tenant they own. What: a keyless `host.*` call mints a tenant (`implicit_signup_and_dispatch`, `src/handler.rs:8065-8206`) and `signup` mints one on request; nothing ends either. The 10-20 prod read in PRD-mcphost-implicit-signup-mints-only-on-success counted 2657 live implicit tenants with zero successful calls and 47 external implicit tenants in 30 days. Why they cannot fix it: `host.self_offboard` needs the tenant's credential, which an abandoned agent no longer presents; `admin.tenant_disable` and `admin.tenant_delete` (`src/admin.rs:166`) are hand actions on prod data that need Joe's word each time. Cost: unbounded growth of rows that count as users in every funnel and PMF query, plus the exact risk Joe's amendment names: a key that vanishes with...
user_persona: An agent that calls host.sync.create with a source ref and gets a scheduled mirror in one call; Operator Joe who reads docs/tools.md and llms.txt and knows both were rendered from the SourceKind enum.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given an external implicit tenant, an external `signup` tenant, a claimed one and a synthetic one, When `host.doctor` and `admin.tenants` are read, the first makes one call, and both are read again, Then both external rows show `tenant_lifecycle.policy = "external_unclaimed"`, `idle_since_unix = MAX(COALESCE(last_seen_unix, created_unix), floor_unix)` and `idle_days`, the call moves the first's clock, and the other two show `policy: null`.

Given subject A idle 20 days with one claim attempt and subject B idle 20 days with none, When the sweep runs twice on day 20 and once on day 21, Then one `FakeEmailClient` send goes to A's newest `claim_codes.email`, naming 10 days left and A's claim URL, without A's key or `/u/` secret, A's `claim_expires_at` is `idle_since + 44 d`, A has one `warned` and B two `warn_no_address` events, and runs two and three send nothing.

Given A idle 30 days with a `warned` event 10 days old, C idle 30 days whose first warn attempt is 3 days old, and D claimed at idle day 25, When the sweep runs, Then only A ends `disabled_reason = 'unclaimed_expired'`, torn down once, one notice sent, its `/u/` URL reading `tenant_disabled` with the reason and `claim_url` and its key `tenant_key_invalid`; C and D are untouched, and a keyless call from a new peer still mints.

Given A invalidated 5 days ago and E at idle day 30 whose claim verification a test hook interleaves between the sweep's two phases, When A's emailed URL is verified by its bound address and tried with another, Then A is restored (`disabled = 0`, reason and `claim_bound_email` `NULL`, `owner_verified_at` set, one `restored` event), the other address is refused, and E ends claimed and enabled, never claimed-and-disabled.

Given subjects invalidated 14, 13 and 20 days ago, the 20-day one re-enabled by `admin.tenant_enable`, When the sweep runs, Then only the 14-day row is deleted through `delete_tenant`'s body with an `admin_events` row `tenant_purge_expired`, the 13-day row waits, the re-enabled row has `last_seen_unix` reset and is neither purged nor re-invalidated, and `admin.funnel` reports both `tenants_unclaimed_*` counts after a restart.

Given fixtures idle 60 days carrying each `EXT` exclusion marker, a pre-floor fixture P with `floor_unix` 1 day ago, and a subject under env var `off`, When the sweep runs with every stage due, Then no fixture gains an event, email, flag or deletion, `prune_log` reports `pre_floor.count = 1` with P in `dry_run`, and a second sweep with `floor_unix` 20 days ago gives P one `warned` or `warn_no_address` event and no `invalidated` one.

Given the email provider failing both attempts for A at idle day 20, When the sweep runs on days 20, 21 and 30, Then day 20 writes `warn_failed` with the provider status plus a `claim_email_events` row, day 21 retries and writes `warned`, day 30 invalidates A because its first attempt is 10 days old, and `prune_log.deleted_json` carries every stage count and `pre_floor` under `external_unclaimed_tenants`.

Given prod after this change deploys, When the contract is fetched anonymously, Then it carries the external policy from the binary's constants (Live; evidence: `curl -sS https://mcphost.dev/contract.json | jq -e '.tenant_lifecycle.external_unclaimed | .idle_days == 30 and .warn_lead_days == 10 and .purge_grace_days == 14 and .disabled_reason == "unclaimed_expired" and .selector.origin == "external"'`)

scope: src/sync/mod.rs: the SourceKind registry, host.sync.create/list/get/delete/run_now, and the trigger tick's sync pass writing a not_implemented sync_runs receipt.
migrations/0130_syncs.sql: syncs and sync_runs tables; Plan.syncs_max (free 5, pro 50) and the quota_syncs_max, connection_missing and schedule_too_frequent error codes.
www/llms.txt gains a generated Data sync section and docs/tools.md the source.kind enum, both rendered from SourceKind.
non_goals: Fetching rows (the pull PRD); push or conflict handling (the two-way PRD); type inference beyond text columns; any new OAuth flow.

additional.main_database_tables: syncs and sync_runs live in the main database (migration 0130), not a per-tenant file, so the tick's sync pass is one indexed query across tenants.

five_whys_trace.q: Why can an agent not keep a host table equal to a sheet?
five_whys_trace.a: No verb registers an external source; the agent would own a puller, a token and a diff loop.
host.table.append cannot update a row and host.trigger.set only calls a published tool.
One SourceKind enum generates the schema, docs and dispatch, so the five kinds cannot drift.

ambiguities_resolved.question: What is source.secret?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: The NAME of a host.secret (stored as secret_name), never a value, so no secret-named field exists on a Debug struct.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Do push and two_way modes run?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: They are accepted at create with status pending_mode (the PRD default) and the tick skips them.
